items.title: How you met your own reaction
items.prompt: When you noticed your own reaction in {episode_label}, how did you relate to it?

options.text: I wanted to understand what was happening in me.
I could let the reaction be there without rushing to change it.
I judged myself for reacting that way.
I wanted the reaction gone.
I was caught up in it, rather than noticing it from any distance.
I only noticed my reaction afterward.
I did not notice a reaction I can describe.

confounds: Curiosity, patience, judgment and noticing late concern stance toward this reaction; none alone establishes Self leadership.
Missing or unselected information remains unknown.
items.authoring_note: Samples the relationship to a reaction, which ordinary calm, competence, or receiving help cannot establish.
items.purpose: Samples the relationship to a reaction, which ordinary calm, competence, or receiving help cannot establish.

items.title: Awareness and room to choose
items.prompt: While noticing that reaction, how much room did you have to choose what happened next?

options.text: I could feel the reaction and still consider different responses.
I noticed it, but still felt driven to act one way.
I got distance by dismissing what I felt.
I felt detached from the situation, rather than more able to choose.
I could reflect on it only after the moment had passed.

confounds: Distance that increases choice differs from suppression or felt detachment; hindsight does not establish choice during the moment.
Missing or unselected information remains unknown.
items.authoring_note: Distinguishes awareness, room for choice, retrospective reflection, dismissal and felt detachment; none alone yields a Self score.
items.purpose: Distinguishes awareness, room for choice, retrospective reflection, dismissal and felt detachment; none alone yields a Self score.

items.title: Why it was hard to acknowledge
items.prompt: What made it difficult to acknowledge that feeling or need to yourself in {episode_label}?

options.text: It felt wrong for me to feel or need that.
I was afraid the feeling would become too much.
I worried that acknowledging it would make it harder to control what I did.
I could not make sense of what I was feeling.
There was too much to deal with just then.
Acknowledging it was not difficult; something else was.

confounds: Identification difficulty, time pressure and internal prohibition differ; no single response establishes an exile.
Missing or unselected information remains unknown.
items.authoring_note: Resolves internal exclusion versus temporary demands or difficulty identifying experience, after an actual admission difficulty.
items.purpose: Resolves internal exclusion versus temporary demands or difficulty identifying experience, after an actual admission difficulty.

items.title: Returning to what was set aside
items.prompt: Later in {episode_label}, what happened to the feeling or need you had struggled to acknowledge?

options.text: I came back to it and could give it some room.
It came up again and I pushed it away.
It was still there, but I still found it difficult to allow.
It faded without my doing anything in particular.
I did not get another chance to attend to it.
I cannot recall a later part of that situation.

confounds: Delayed acknowledgment can reflect temporary practical demands; later absence is not proof the feeling was exiled.
Missing or unselected information remains unknown.
items.authoring_note: Separates temporary postponement, later access, persistence and disappearance without requiring a hidden-part story.
items.purpose: Separates temporary postponement, later access, persistence and disappearance without requiring a hidden-part story.

items.title: What the response changed inside
items.prompt: In {episode_label}, how did {response_label} affect your access to what you were feeling or wanting?

options.text: I could tell more clearly what I felt or wanted.
I could still feel it, but it was easier to stay with.
I became less aware of it.
I still knew what I felt; I was showing less of it.
It became harder to ignore.
I did not notice a change.
I cannot tell whether that response changed it.

confounds: Reduced display, reduced awareness and increased tolerance are different effects; effect is not proof of an intended motive.
Missing or unselected information remains unknown.
items.authoring_note: Links an actual response to internal access without assuming that outward concealment removes internal access.
items.purpose: Links an actual response to internal access without assuming that outward concealment removes internal access.

items.title: How convincing a self-conclusion felt
items.prompt: How convincing did that conclusion about yourself feel at the time?

options.text: It felt like a fact I could not argue with.
Part of me questioned it, but it still pulled strongly.
It was one possible explanation, not a settled truth.
It applied to that mistake, not to me as a whole.
I noticed the thought but did not believe it.

confounds: A strongly held current self-conclusion has no automatically inferred childhood origin; an episode-bound thought is not a global belief.
Missing or unselected information remains unknown.
items.authoring_note: Tests the current force and scope of an organizing belief; this does not establish a historical burden or origin.
items.purpose: Tests the current force and scope of an organizing belief; this does not establish a historical burden or origin.

items.title: Whether the self-conclusion changed
items.prompt: Did anything later in that mistake episode change how you saw yourself?

options.text: What happened gave me reason to revise the conclusion.
Something went better, but I treated it as an exception or luck.
I could see another interpretation, but the original conclusion still felt true.
The conclusion stayed the same even after the mistake was handled.
Nothing relevant happened that would test it.
The situation was still unfinished when I last thought about it.

confounds: Remembered evidence and belief revision do not prove an objectively false self-appraisal or its developmental cause.
Missing or unselected information remains unknown.
items.authoring_note: Collects reported updating or non-updating rather than assuming a belief resists contrary evidence.
items.purpose: Collects reported updating or non-updating rather than assuming a belief resists contrary evidence.

items.title: Something you kept to yourself
items.prompt: Think of a recent moment when you kept a reaction or wish to yourself. What did you hold back?

options.text: Anger or a wish to push back.
Hurt or sadness.
A wish for help or care.
Excitement or pride in something.
An interest or ambition I wanted to pursue.
An opinion I wanted to express.

confounds: Keeping pride, ambition, anger or care private is not itself internal exclusion.
Missing or unselected information remains unknown.
items.authoring_note: A user-selected new episode extends beyond hurt and need to anger, pride, interests and voice. Keeping something private is not itself evidence of an exile.
items.purpose: A user-selected new episode extends beyond hurt and need to anger, pride, interests and voice. Keeping something private is not itself evidence of an exile.

items.title: What shaped keeping it private
items.prompt: What most shaped keeping that reaction or wish to yourself?

options.text: I wanted to keep it private.
There was a better time or place for it.
There were practical consequences to showing it.
I expected a response I did not want.
It felt wrong for me to have that feeling or wish.
Letting myself feel it fully seemed too much.

confounds: Privacy, timing and realistic consequences remain ordinary explanations, not disguised pathology.
Missing or unselected information remains unknown.
items.authoring_note: Separates external consequences, chosen privacy, timing and internal prohibition in a volunteered actual episode.
items.purpose: Separates external consequences, chosen privacy, timing and internal prohibition in a volunteered actual episode.

items.title: Private acknowledgment
items.prompt: Even without showing it, how much room did you give that reaction or wish inside?

options.text: I could acknowledge it and let myself feel it.
I intended to return to it when I had room.
I tried not to let myself feel it.
I was hard on myself for having it.
I found it difficult to tell what I actually felt.
It changed or faded without my trying to push it away.

confounds: Private acknowledgment can coexist with withholding expression; internal difficulty is a current description rather than a diagnosis.
Missing or unselected information remains unknown.
items.authoring_note: Directly tests internal permission rather than upgrading outward concealment into an exile.
items.purpose: Directly tests internal permission rather than upgrading outward concealment into an exile.

items.title: Giving two wants room
items.prompt: In that moment of wanting {first_want} and {second_want}, what happened when you tried to listen to both?

options.text: Both concerns became clearer without my having to choose immediately.
I could find room for some of each.
One pull became louder when I attended to the other.
I dismissed one so I could get on with the other.
I could not keep both in mind.
I did not try to listen to both in that moment.

confounds: Two wishes are not automatically polarized parts; allowing both is not a measured Self score.
Missing or unselected information remains unknown.
items.authoring_note: Samples actual internal engagement, not an instruction to perform an exercise; not trying is a valid endpoint.
items.purpose: Samples actual internal engagement, not an instruction to perform an exercise; not trying is a valid endpoint.

items.title: Whether the concerns were shared
items.prompt: Looking back at those two pulls, how did their concerns fit together?

options.text: They were trying to avoid the same thing in different ways.
They were concerned about different outcomes.
One was about avoiding something; the other was simply something I wanted.
Neither felt like an attempt to avoid something.

confounds: Reported shared concern does not prove a shared Exile or identical part identity.
Missing or unselected information remains unknown.
items.authoring_note: Records a perceived relation between two actual concerns without turning a shared word into a shared Exile or separate entities.
items.purpose: Records a perceived relation between two actual concerns without turning a shared word into a shared Exile or separate entities.

items.title: Continuity beyond a matching action
items.prompt: Across those two moments, what felt continuous besides the outward response?

options.text: The same concern kept coming up.
I felt held to the same expectation of myself.
The same feeling was difficult to stay with.
The outward response matched, but the experience behind it felt different.
Only the outward response seemed the same.
I cannot make that comparison.

confounds: Same action in two episodes does not establish same function or same part; continuity is the reported comparison.
Missing or unselected information remains unknown.
items.authoring_note: A distinct-occurrence comparison follows a reported matched action. Identity remains an interpretation, not a literal part count.
items.purpose: A distinct-occurrence comparison follows a reported matched action. Identity remains an interpretation, not a literal part count.

items.title: Whether the earlier response returned
items.prompt: After {next_response_label}, did your earlier response return before that same situation ended?

options.text: I went back to the earlier response.
I wanted to go back to it, but did not.
I did not return to it.
The situation ended before there was a chance to return.

Missing or unselected information remains unknown.
items.authoring_note: Records an actual return rather than calling every two-step sequence a loop. Return has a new step identity, not a cyclic chronology.
items.purpose: Records an actual return rather than calling every two-step sequence a loop. Return has a new step identity, not a cyclic chronology.

items.title: What preceded the return
items.prompt: What was happening just before you went back to that earlier response?

options.text: The original issue was still unresolved.
Something about my next move had left another problem.
The other person responded in a way that drew me back in.

confounds: What preceded a return may be relevant without being its unique cause.
Missing or unselected information remains unknown.
items.authoring_note: Describes the reported conditions before a return; not proof of the unique cause of a feedback loop.
items.purpose: Describes the reported conditions before a return; not proof of the unique cause of a feedback loop.

items.title: What remained available

options.text: Take in new information.

Carry out a familiar task.

Missing or unselected information remains unknown.
items.authoring_note: Samples a remaining capability without pretending an unselected capability was absent or measuring total state range.
items.purpose: Samples a remaining capability without pretending an unselected capability was absent or measuring total state range.

items.title: What showed and what was happening inside

options.text: I looked steady while feeling strained inside.

items.purpose: Records the respondent’s own estimate of presentation; not an observer measurement or evidence that the body is the hidden truth.

items.title: How the change unfolded

items.authoring_note: Describes remembered onset without inferring objective speed, cause, thresholds or body-first precedence.
items.purpose: Describes remembered onset without inferring objective speed, cause, thresholds or body-first precedence.

items.purpose: Distinguishes resuming activity from recovery in other channels without assuming an unseen residual cost.

items.purpose: A coarse recalled interval, not a physiological recovery latency, treatment target or exact threshold.

items.purpose: A remembered channel comparison, not a required recovery ladder or measured physiology.

items.purpose: Preserves changing circumstances instead of attributing every improvement to an internal strategy.
